title: Raised Above Kings and Stars
english: …perceiving that his word held some hidden meaning, they followed him (Matthew 4:20). At once they rose above the earth and were seen to be more glorious than kings: like angels, ministers of God, heralds of salvation, servants of immortality, more radiant than sun, moon, and stars. For their glory is not, as it were, beneath the heavens, but above the…
translator_notes: The section begins mid-sentence: its subject and first participles ('heeding the one who called them, made firm by faith, and…') close the previous section, and the opening ellipsis marks the join.
'His word' is Christ's saying 'I will make you fishers of men', which the apostles did not dismiss as idle talk; ἀπόκρυφον is rendered 'a hidden meaning'.
τῆς γῆς ἄνω γεγόνασι: literally 'they came to be above the earth'; rendered 'they rose above the earth'.
ἀθανασίας διάκονοι: 'servants of immortality' keeps διάκονος as service rather than the church office.

'Their glory' is the apostles', set above that of the heavenly lights just named. The comparison with sun and stars may echo Daniel 12:3 or Matthew 13:43, but the wording is not close enough to cite inline.
The section ends mid-phrase ('above the…'); the word 'heavens' opens the next section.
baehrens: PG 93; In sanctum Andream (Khazarzar) u02 rem early

title: Praying for the Apostles' Light
english: …heavens. They have a light that cannot be quenched, a course that never ceases, rays that always shine; let us pray that these may shine into our minds. Let us flee the darkness itself, turn aside from the bitter brine of life, and, as we travel the restless sea, escape the surge of the soul-destroying waves, and…
translator_notes: The section opens by completing the previous sentence ('…above the heavens'); 'they' are the apostles.
'Let us pray' renders an exhortation (εὐξώμεθα): the rays of the apostles' light are asked to shine into our minds.
The section ends mid-sentence; the next section continues '…let us become fish in the heavenly net'.
baehrens: PG 93; In sanctum Andream (Khazarzar) u02 rem mid

title: Fish for the Master's Table
english: …let us become fish in the heavenly net of Christ's unlettered apostles, choice fare for the Master's table, at which the King of kings (1 Timothy 6:15) dines, counting our salvation as his food. To him be glory and might for ever and ever. Amen.
translator_notes: The section begins mid-sentence: 'let us become' continues the string of exhortations in the previous section, whose English ends '…waves, and…'.

'Christ's unlettered apostles' takes up the homily's earlier theme of the unlettered fishermen: the wise who hurry to the unlettered man as to a teacher, and Christ's choice of 'the poor, the untaught, the unlettered, and fishermen'. Acts 4:13 calls Peter and John unlettered (ἀγράμματοι); it is a possible echo, not cited inline.
τῆς ἄνω σαγήνης: 'the heavenly net', the net from above, playing on the call to be fishers of men; a possible echo of the dragnet parable (Matthew 13:47), not cited inline.
ὄψα: cooked relish eaten with bread, very often fish; 'choice fare' keeps the fish image.
'The Master's table' is capitalised because the Master is Christ.
'Counting our salvation as his food' may recall John 4:34 ('My food is to do the will of him who sent me'), but the wording differs, so it is not cited inline.
The closing doxology is the standard ending of a homily (compare 1 Peter 4:11; Revelation 1:6) and is not cited inline.
